import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a logical order for age groups to ensure consistent plotting
age_group_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']
df['customer_age_group'] = pd.Categorical(df['customer_age_group'], categories=age_group_order, ordered=True)

# Aggregate total sales by product and customer age group
# This will allow us to see which products are popular among different age demographics
sales_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Sort by product and then by age group for consistent plotting order
sales_by_product_age = sales_by_product_age.sort_values(by=['product', 'customer_age_group'])

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create a grouped bar plot to visualize total sales by product and customer age group
sns.barplot(
    data=sales_by_product_age,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='customer_age_group',
    palette='viridis',  # A perceptually uniform colormap
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Sales by Product Across Customer Age Groups', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Product Type', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)

# Rotate x-axis labels if product names are long to prevent overlap
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend to differentiate the age groups, placing it outside the plot area
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Improve layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.98, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure as a high-resolution PNG file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
